elements.element: Renewal mechanics must be either renewal only by mutual written agreement or automatic renewal for successive 12-month terms.
elements.evidence: The clause uses the permitted automatic-renewal alternative and specifies that each additional term is 12 months.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Customer must be able to opt out on 30 days' written notice before the end of the current term.
elements.evidence: Either party, which includes Customer, may prevent renewal by giving at least 30 days' written notice before the current term ends.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Vendor must remind Customer of the upcoming renewal at least 60 days before the end of the current term.
elements.evidence: IBM must notify Customer of the upcoming renewal at least 60 days before the current term ends.

elements.element: Renewal-term price increases must be capped at the lesser of the increase in CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that renewal Charges will not increase by more than the lesser of the increase in CPI and 3% over the expiring-term Charges.

elements.element: The clause may provide for automatic renewal.
elements.evidence: Each Service Option Attachment renews automatically unless timely notice is given.

elements.element: The non-renewal notice window for an automatic renewal must be no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least 30 days' advance written notice, which is within the maximum 60-day window.

elements.element: Renewal-term price increases must not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: The lesser-of-CPI-and-3% cap necessarily limits any renewal increase to no more than 3%, and therefore no more than 5%.

result.reason: The operative redline fully implements the preferred automatic-renewal route: fixed 12-month renewals, a 30-day Customer opt-out, a 60-day IBM reminder, and the required CPI/3% price cap. It also exceeds the fallback protections. The changes are confined to renewal mechanics and pricing, preserve the surrounding term language, and introduce no contradiction. Drafting is effective, though the phrase “notifies the other party by at least 30 days' written notice” is slightly awkward; “gives the other party at least 30 days' prior written notice” would be cleaner.
